notes: Each eval hands the skill one recommendation object from docs/research/sota_agents_research/sota_agents.v1.json and asks for the agent to be built. Expectations assert on the artifact set and on the four verdict-design decisions, not on exact wording — two competent runs will name an id differently and both be right. Each eval should run in a workspace copy of the repo, since building an agent writes into policy/, tests/ and docs/.

evals.name: deterministic-agent-built-and-executed
evals.prompt: Our curriculum pipeline shipped four lessons where the renderer dumped raw JSON as the lesson body and nothing caught it. The SOTA scan in docs/research/sota_agents_research/sota_agents.v1.json recommends a 'Structured-Output Rendering Conformance Gate' for exactly this. Build that agent into the repo properly.
evals.expected_output: A complete agent artifact set: a failure-ledger entry, a check-inventory entry in the engine's inventory, a release surface, an accept/reject fixture pair where the reject fixture is a unit whose child-facing section is a serialized object, a detector plus a registered gate that executes against that pair, an RT- obligation recording that no rendered subject exists, and a dossier carrying the recommendation's sources verbatim.
expectations: The check id is added to policy/checks.v1.yaml, not to a curriculum's inventory, because the check asserts a shape rather than anything subject-specific.

The inventory entry carries exactly one of verified_by or deferred, and whichever it carries resolves — a verified_by to a gate id present in tests/gates/registry.py, a deferred to an id in policy/deferred.v1.yaml.
A corresponding entry is added to policy/failures.v1.yaml describing the raw-JSON defect, and it names the new check id in a checks list.
A reject fixture is created under tests/fixtures/ in which a child-facing section actually parses as a JSON object or array — it reproduces the named defect rather than being generically malformed.
An accept fixture is created that differs from the reject fixture only in that the defect is removed.
The gate registration asserts a specific expected_error string on the reject fixture, not merely that the fixture fails.
The agent is built as a deterministic check that blocks, and the run states why a judge was not used for a defect a parser settles.

The gate's summary line reports the count of real generated units scanned (zero today) and cites the RT- obligation that records why it is zero, rather than reporting fixture coverage as coverage of generated work.
A dossier is written at docs/agents/<CHECK-ID>.md carrying the recommendation's what_makes_it_sota text and its source URLs, attributed to the scan and explicitly marked as not re-verified.
No new web search or source fetch is performed — the sources are carried across from the recommendation unchanged and none are added.
scripts/validate_agent.py is run against the new check id and reports no failures.

evals.name: conflict-with-existing-decision-is-surfaced
evals.prompt: Please implement the first recommendation from docs/research/sota_agents_research/sota_agents.v1.json — the Cross-Family Structured Judge Panel — in our repo.
evals.expected_output: The run discovers that this repo already retired a multi-judge panel with recorded measurements and already has REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY, surfaces that conflict explicitly, amends the existing id rather than adding a competing one, and designs the verdict as flagging rather than blocking given the reported judge bias.
expectations: The run reads policy/checks.v1.yaml and finds the existing REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY entry before creating anything.

The conflict between the recommendation's judge panel and this repo's recorded decision to retire a twelve-judge panel is stated explicitly, citing the repo's own measurements (effective votes, cost, deterministic checks outperforming judges).
The existing check id is amended rather than a second competing judge id being added alongside it.
The reconciliation — what the recommendation argues, what the repo already decided, and which evidence won — is written into the dossier rather than left in conversation.
The verdict is designed to flag or to escalate rather than to block, and the reason given is the unreliability of judge verdicts rather than an unexplained preference.
The model-call cost is reconciled against policy/limits.v1.yaml per_lab.max_model_calls rather than being left unbudgeted.
No limit value in policy/limits.v1.yaml is raised to accommodate the agent; if it does not fit, that is recorded as a finding.
The execution status is honest: if no second model family is available to this repo today, the entry is deferred with a blocked_by that names that, rather than claiming a gate executes it.

evals.name: curriculum-scoped-placement-and-safety-verdict
evals.prompt: Build the Domain-Fact Safeguard Reviewer from our SOTA scan (docs/research/sota_agents_research/sota_agents.v1.json) — it's meant to catch wrong domain claims like the multimeter fuse-sharing behaviour that nothing currently verifies.
evals.expected_output: An agent whose subject is one curriculum's domain facts, correctly placed in that curriculum's own check inventory with its own release surface, with a safety-relevant judged verdict designed to escalate to a human rather than to block, and an honest execution status.
expectations: The check is added to curricula/arduino_kit/checks.v1.yaml rather than to policy/checks.v1.yaml, and the reason given is that its subject is one curriculum's files or subject-specific claims.
A release row in that curriculum's inventory advertises the new id at the stage the entry declares, or the run confirms an existing wildcard pattern already covers it.
The run distinguishes this check from the existing DOMAIN-VERIFIER / DOMAIN-SCHEMA-VALID checks, which confirm schema validity rather than factual correctness.
Because the verdict is a model judgement on safety-relevant content, the design escalates to a named human reviewer rather than silently blocking, and the reasoning for that choice is recorded.
The asserts string states plainly whether the check blocks or flags, so a report quoting it cannot over-read it.
The execution status is deferred with a truthful blocked_by, or verified by a gate that executes against a fixture pair — never advertised as executed with nothing behind it.
The reject fixture encodes an actually-wrong domain claim of the kind the recommendation names, not a schema violation.
The dossier carries the recommendation's two source URLs verbatim, attributed to the scan, with no additional sources introduced.
